Subject: NovusHealth - ask for exec authority on latency tolerance + remedy cap

Hi Lauren / Ben,

Quick summary: NovusHealth is moving from pilot to production for their AI summarization feature and needs us to sign a 12-month expansion. Procurement pushed back on our standard latency SLO (p95 target 300ms) and is requesting a toleration at p95=500ms for the first 12 months plus a hard cap on service credits. They also want a one-time concession on commercial terms (20% ARR discount if we accept this SLA variance).

Attached: novus_request_summary.pdf and SLA-draft-v3.docx.

What's needed from leadership:
- Approval to accept p95 latency tolerance = 500ms for 12 months (non-standard).
- Authorization to cap service credits at $40k (customer asks $50k; deal desk recommended $40k).
- Sign-off for conditional 20% annual commitment discount (contingent on amendment + 12-month commitment).

Timeline: customer expects an answer by EOD Friday (12/17). We can retain close if we get an executive greenlight.

Ask: Can one of you authorize this exception or route to the right approver? If approved, I will start Amendment + DocuSign flow and loop Legal for redlines.

Thanks,

Thanks for the ping. Technical assessment (short):
- We can safely relax p95 from 300ms to 500ms for a transitional period if the workload profile is known and we enable prefix caching + KV cache priming.
- Risk: longer-term tolerance may mask regressions; recommend a 12-week phased monitoring window with weekly thresholds. If we see more than 3 breach incidents in a rolling quarter, we revert to standard SLOs or trigger a remediation plan.

Suggested operational commitments to include in the amendment:
- Redwood will implement prefix/KV caching and a monthly performance snapshot to Novus.
- If we exceed 3 major latency incidents in any quarter, the tolerance is revoked and we resume standard terms.
- We also recommend a $40k cap on credits (rather than $50k) to limit exposure.

Please include these conditions if Legal is drafting. I'm comfortable recommending exec approval conditioned on the monitoring & rollback clause.

-Rishi

Team — after reviewing the ask and the recommendations from CS and Finance, I approve the following exception for NovusHealth, effective upon execution of an amendment:

1) Latency p95 tolerance: increase to 500ms (from 300ms) for a term of up to 12 months.
2) Service credit cap: $40,000 aggregate for the 12-month period.
3) Commercial concession: up to 20% ARR discount contingent on a signed 12-month commitment and execution of the amendment.
4) Conditions: Redwood will implement the operational mitigations listed by Rishi (prefix/KV caching, weekly performance snapshots). If we exceed 3 major latency incidents in a rolling quarter, the tolerance is revoked and standard SLOs + remedies apply.
5) Review cadence: 30-day post-amendment operational review; Legal must finalize amendment language and start DocuSign.

Marissa — proceed with DocuSign (link below). Jonas/Rishi — prepare the monitoring dashboard and a plain-English clause for Legal describing the rollback trigger.
